Fed’s Goolsbee says he sees no clear path back to 2% inflation
body: Goolsbee’s comments on inflation, interest rates and AI investment crossed the wires.

The takeaway is hawkish. Goolsbee sees a sizable demand component to inflation, which makes it harder for the Fed to look through the recent price pressure. Businesses are already reporting higher costs where they compete with data centers for components, and he sees a risk that the economy has trouble absorbing the current pace of investment without overheating.

Services inflation is the barometer to watch. If it stays sticky even as energy pressures ease, that would strengthen the case that demand is keeping inflation elevated and give the Fed more reason to tighten. If services inflation cools, the case for a steeper rate path weakens.

news.title: AUDUSD moves to a new low.   Price action is ping ponging down and up and back down again.
body: Australia’s October jobs report was considerably weaker than expected. Employment fell 43,500 against the 25,500 gain expected in our preview, and the unemployment rate rose to 4.9% versus 4.7% expected. September’s job loss was revised to 36,400 from 39,300, putting the two-month decline at nearly 80,000 jobs, the biggest in five years.

The rise in unemployment alongside a drop in participation is the detail that stands out. A smaller share of Australians were working or looking for work, and even with that decline in participation, more people were unemployed. The ABS’s smoothed trend measure still showed a modest gain of 7,200 jobs, but trend unemployment also rose, to 4.8%.

The RBA raised its cash rate by 25 basis points to 4.85% earlier this month and warned that inflation would stay elevated for longer. The jobs report strengthens the case for a hold on December 8. Reuters reported that traders unwound bets on further hikes and priced in roughly 45 basis points of easing by the end of 2027, about double what they had priced before the release

The AUDUSD initially fell sharply from 0.67202 to near 0.6660 after the weaker-than-expected Australian jobs report. Buyers came back in and erased nearly the entire decline, taking the pair back toward the Asian session high at 0.6720 early in North American trading.

That rebound did not last. As U.S. stocks reversed their early gains, traders turned their attention back to U.S. inflation concerns and still-solid jobs data. Sellers took control again, retracing the entire bounce and extending the move to a new session low at 0.66562. The pair is trading at 0.66624 as the North American session winds down.

The session low at 0.66562 dipped just below the 200-week moving average at 0.66575. The price is back above it for now, putting the focus on where the pair closes the week. A weekly close below 0.66575 would give sellers more control and increase the potential for further downside.

If buyers can hold above that moving average and build on the bounce, the 100-week moving average at 0.67043 is the first key topside target. Getting back above it would give buyers more room to make a run at the session high near 0.6720.

news.title: Peterson: The Fed's chairman sees an AI revolution coming. Now he has to figure out what it means
body: Artificial intelligence is about to sweep through the economy. The Federal Reserve is bracing for impact.

"We are at a hinge point in the U.S. economy," Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh said at a conference he convened in San Francisco on Monday. But exactly when and how the economy could turn, and what that means for interest rates and inflation, isn't yet clear.

The meeting of Warsh's AI task force saw the new Fed chairman publicly asking the questions Americans will ultimately expect him to answer. He hinted at a few of his private views on whether white-collar workers could soon face massive job losses, but he largely left the speculation to an array of experts he has assembled to advise the Fed.

With the technology racing ahead, Warsh won't be able to put off giving his own answers much longer. AI lab Anthropic plans to price the shares for its initial public offering on Wednesday and could raise as much as $64 billion at a $1.4 trillion valuation. Vast spending from AI firms is prompting the Fed to contemplate raising interest rates in December to slow down the rate of price increases as the tech sector heats up the economy.

Meanwhile Americans are souring on some aspects of the technology. The Nov. 3 midterms saw voters enact an array of state-level measures to slow down construction of the data centers that are essential to powering AI.

Warsh moderated three out of four sessions at Monday's event and was involved in selecting the speakers. Among them was one of the few prominent Democrats who was willing to speak out against that anti-data center trend.

It is "a very troubling sign" that so many anti-data center measures passed in the midterms, Gina Raimondo said. She is a former secretary of Commerce under President Joe Biden and a former governor of Rhode Island.
Stopping AI "would be very bad for America" and for the people who voted for the measures, Raimondo said.
Warsh didn't say whether he shares that view, and how it would translate into monetary policy isn't exactly clear.

The event was an unusual one for the Fed. The central bank employs a small army of Ph.D. economists who can rapidly weigh in on anything affecting the U.S. and global economies. But in keeping with his long-standing critiques of the Fed as insular and outdated, Warsh has chosen to draw expertise from outside the institution to help it figure out how to think about what AI will do to productivity and jobs.
Warsh has assembled a task force on that issue, alongside four others devoted to aspects of Fed policymaking.

The public heard Monday from one of the three official members of the task force: venture capitalist Marc Andreessen. Warsh went to Stanford University with Andreessen's wife, and the two have been longtime friends. Another task force member, Stanford economist Chad Jones, is on leave and working at Anthropic and couldn't speak during the company's blackout period ahead of the IPO. The third, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma, didn't attend the event.

Andreessen is hugely optimistic about the promise of AI as a technology, but believes the government won't let Americans experience its full effects. Heavy regulation in areas such as healthcare and education mean technology can't replace people's jobs in those sectors, he said.

"To the extent our economy is a free market economy, then maybe you could see the, let's say, extremely rapid displacement scenarios people are talking about," Andreessen said. "But we've mostly outlawed the kind of job transition that … both the utopians the doomers talk about."

news.title: Canada seeks interim U.S. tariff deal by year-end, CBC reports
body: CBC News reported, citing sources familiar with Thursday’s meeting between Canada-U.S. Trade Minister Dominic LeBlanc and the federal government’s Canada-U.S. economic advisory committee, that Ottawa is aiming for an interim tariff agreement with the Trump administration. CBC News

The year-end target gives CAD traders a date to watch. The first test is whether the two sides can put terms in writing. From there, the scope matters. Relief across steel, aluminum, autos and lumber could ease cost pressure for Canadian exporters and give the Canadian dollar some support. The details to watch are which tariffs come down, by how much and when.

Looking at the USDCAD on the hourly chart below, the price today did fall below the 100 hour MA and a swing area in the 1.42198 to 1.42986 area. However, momentum could not be sustained below that key break and the price has pushed higher. Earlier in the day, the price reached the highest level since April 2025 at 1.43566. That is the next target with close risk now at the rising 100 hour MA at 1.4302. Move above 1.43566 and traders will look toward the swing highs from March 19, 2025 and April 1, 2025 at 1.4401 to 1.44145 (not shown).

news.title: GBPUSD breaks to a new 2026 low. The daily chart shows room to the downside.
body: The GBPUSD is trading to a new low for 2026 as inflation concerns push the greenback higher. The move lower gathered momentum after sellers leaned against resistance on the hourly chart. On the daily chart, the break below a key floor gives sellers room to probe lower.
The GBPUSD is breaking below the daily swing area between 1.31386 and 1.31786. The move also takes the price further away from 1.31926, the 38.2% retracement of the rally from the January 2025 low.

The lower edge of the old floor near 1.3139 is the first barometer on a bounce. If the price stays below it, sellers keep the downside bias. A move back into the swing area would take some of the momentum out of the break. Buyers would then need to work through the upper end of the area and get back above 1.31926 to give themselves more breathing room.

On the downside, the next daily swing area comes in between 1.2998 and 1.3046. The top of that area at 1.3046 is the first target. Below that, the focus shifts toward 1.2998 and then 1.29838, the 50% midpoint of the rally from the January 2025 low.

Drilling down to the hourly chart above, the rebound off the earlier low stalled near 1.3171, the lower edge of a swing area that extends to 1.31808. The 100-hour moving average sits within that area near 1.31797, adding to the resistance.

Sellers leaned against the bottom of the area and were rewarded with a push to fresh lows. That gives traders a sequence to watch on the next bounce. A move above 1.3171 would be the first sign that buyers are making a play. Getting and staying above the 100-hour moving average and 1.31808 would give that move more credibility.

For now, the daily chart shows where the price has room to go, and the hourly chart shows where sellers can define their risk. With the pair making new lows for the year, the burden of proof remains on the buyers.

news.title: Trump weighs another strike on Iran as Hormuz shipping risks mount. Returns to Washington after overseas trip.
body: Geopolitics is building as President Trump is heading back to Washington after wrapping up talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen. Ukraine was a focus coming out of the meetings.

Trump said he and Xi agreed that Iran should fully reopen the Strait of Hormuz and should not acquire a nuclear weapon. Trump also urged China to help end the war in Ukraine. Beijing’s readout emphasized Taiwan and Xi’s call for better communication on trade and economic issues.

Ukraine came up in Trump’s one-on-one with Putin and again in the three-way talks. Afterward, US envoy Jared Kushner said Russia was comfortable with the idea of NATO-style security guarantees for Ukraine. Putin separately ruled out direct talks with Kyiv, citing Ukraine’s strike on the Kerch Bridge

The leaders agreed to hold talks on reducing nuclear risks and preventing proliferation. They also called for increasing supplies of refined petroleum products and keeping energy flows stable. The joint declaration gave no production targets or timeline and made no mention of either war.

US President Donald Trump is considering another strike on Iran, Israel’s Channel 12 reported, citing an Israeli source. The broadcaster said Trump is in no rush to make a decision and that any strike would be carried out in cooperation with Israel. It said potential targets could include nuclear facilities, infrastructure and senior officials.

US Energy Secretary Chris Wright said Wednesday saw by far the largest flow out of the Strait of Hormuz. Separately, i24NEWS, citing unnamed sources, reported that Iran had become more aggressive in recent days and was using cruise missiles against ships passing through the strait. The report did not provide details on which vessels were affected or whether they sustained damage.

The Houthis also said on Telegram that they would release a statement at 1:30 p.m. ET about what they described as military operations deep inside Saudi Arabia. The announcement itself offered no details about the operations or any impact on energy infrastructure.

For WTI and Brent, the next thing to watch is whether Wednesday’s larger flow through Hormuz can be sustained. Continued improvement would help ease some of the supply concerns. A renewed slowdown in traffic or confirmed damage to energy infrastructure could put the geopolitical risk premium back in focus.

On Ukraine, US special envoy Jared Kushner said Trump came away from the Shenzhen meeting believing peace was achievable. Kushner said there had been progress on a postwar economic plan and that Russia had agreed to engage in a multilateral format with European countries. He added that Trump wants Europe alongside him in reaching a deal.

Kushner said Trump was open to an Article 5-style security guarantee for Ukraine, provided it served US interests. Any agreement would still have to spell out what the US and Europe would commit to if Ukraine came under attack again.

Trump said he was heading back to Washington from China and would hold a White House news conference Friday at noon ET. He said he would also discuss trade deals with Thailand, the Philippines and other countries.

news.title: Fed's Goolsbee: Job market is stable, but inflation is "way higher" than Fed's 2% target
body: Comments from Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee, a 2027 FOMC voter, crossed the wires on inflation, jobs and consumer demand.

The tone is hawkish. If tariffs are still feeding through to prices, one source of inflation may take longer to fade. At the same time, solid consumer demand gives businesses room to pass along higher costs, and a stable job market gives the Fed room to keep its focus on inflation. For traders, the question heading into December is whether the inflation data make the case for a faster pace of tightening.
Remember the Fed did nothing at the end of October meeting most likely due to the elections in early November. The minutes of the meeting were more hawkish yesterday.

In the absence of the election, would the Fed have tightened? My guess is yes. So 50 bps in December would get the Fed to what would be the normal progression given the inflation threat. If the Fed is failing on inflation, do something about it.
The market is still only implying a small 5.6% chance for a 50 bp hike in December (it has been up at about 10% recently).

news.title: USDCAD sellers make a play after a new high for the year
body: The USDCAD has been trending higher since bottoming at 1.3929 in early November. The move to the upside continued in the Asian session today, with the price reaching a new high for the year at 1.43566 (see chart below). That was the highest level going back to April 2025. However, the buyers could not keep the momentum going, and the price rotated back down toward the 100-hour moving average.

That moving average has been a good barometer for the buyers on the way up. The price moved above it on November 5 near 1.3971. On Tuesday, the price came back down to test it near 1.4270, and willing buyers leaned against the level. They could define and limit their risk against the moving average, and the bounce from that test ultimately led to today’s new high.

In the last few hours, the price has traded below the 100-hour moving average, now at 1.4298. That tips the short-term bias in favor of the sellers, but there is more work to do. The moving average is near the top of a swing area between 1.42918 and 1.42990. The sellers need to get and stay below the lower end of that area to give them the go-ahead to push lower.

If they can do that, Tuesday’s low near 1.4270 would be the first target. Remember, that was where buyers leaned against the 100-hour moving average and started the move to today’s high. If the price gets through that low, the rising 200-hour moving average at 1.4248 would be the next target to get to and through.

On the flip side, if the sellers can’t keep the price below the swing area and the pair moves back above 1.42990, the break below the 100-hour moving average starts to look like a failed break. That would give buyers an opening to make another run toward 1.43566.

The price has been above the 200-hour moving average since early November. Getting below the 100-hour moving average gives the sellers a shot. Getting and staying below the 200-hour moving average would give them more control.

On a break below 1.4248, I would look toward the next swing area between 1.41922 and 1.42040. The 38.2% retracement of the move up from 1.3929 to 1.43566 comes in at 1.41933, within that area. That gives buyers another level to lean against if the correction gets that far.

For now, the close risk for sellers is back above 1.42990. On the downside, 1.42918 is the first level sellers need to get through. How the price behaves there will tell us whether they have enough momentum to take a run at the 200-hour moving average.

When a moving average has held on a pullback, I pay attention the next time the price comes back to it. On Tuesday, buyers leaned against the 100-hour moving average near 1.4270. They could define and limit their risk against that level, and the bounce eventually led to a new high for the year. Today, the price moved below that same moving average. That gives sellers a reason to make a play. The next question is whether they can keep the price below it.

This is where the swing area helps. With the 100-hour moving average near the top of the 1.42918–1.42990 area, a move below the average still leaves support at 1.42918. If the price gets below that lower level and then stalls on a bounce back toward it, sellers have a level to lean against and a downside target at Tuesday’s low. If the price instead moves back above 1.42990 and holds, the break starts to look like a failed break, and the reason for leaning short weakens.

Work through the levels one at a time. The break of the 100-hour moving average gives sellers an opening. A break of the swing area gives them room to extend. Getting and staying below the 200-hour moving average would be the next sign that sellers are taking more control.
